blocks.text: A hammer struck on its head transmits a sharp sting into the hand, yet the same blow delivered at one particular spot on a cricket bat or hammer face is almost painless. That spot, and the spin given to a pinned body by a lump of clay thrown at it, are both found by working with impulse and angular momentum rather than forces.

blocks.markdown: For a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis O with moment of inertia $I_O$ (kg m$^2$), Newton's law $\sum M_O=I_O\alpha$ integrates over a short time to the **angular impulse-momentum principle**. The left side is the angular impulse of the moments (N m s) and the right side is the change of angular momentum $H_O=I_O\omega$ (kg m$^2$/s).

blocks.caption: Angular impulse equals change in angular momentum. For a varying torque, the impulse is the area under the torque-time graph.

blocks.title: Flywheel under a torque impulse
blocks.prompt: A flywheel with $I=4.0$ kg m$^2$ turns at 20 rad/s. A motor torque of 45 N m acts for 3 s against a constant friction torque of 5 N m. Find the final angular velocity.
blocks.answer: $\omega_2=50$ rad/s, about 477 rev/min. The result needs no knowledge of the acceleration history.

blocks.markdown: **Body struck by a particle.** When a particle of mass $m_p$ moving at speed $v$ strikes a body pinned at O, the pin applies a large unknown impulsive force, but it passes through O and so has no moment about O. Linear momentum is not conserved (the pin changes it) but **angular momentum about O is**. If the particle hits at a perpendicular distance $d$ from O (so its angular momentum is $m_pvd$) and sticks, the system turns with:

blocks.caption: If the particle rebounds with speed $v'$ instead, $m_pvd+m_pv'd=I_O\omega$ (the particle's angular momentum changes sign).

blocks.title: Clay ball hits a hanging bar
blocks.prompt: A uniform bar (3 kg, 1.2 m long) hangs from a pin at its top end. A 0.2 kg clay ball moving horizontally at 15 m/s hits the bottom end and sticks. Find the angular velocity just after impact.

steps.text: Moment of inertia of the bar about the pin and of the ball about the pin.
Angular momentum of the ball before impact.
Conserve angular momentum about the pin.

blocks.answer: $\omega=2.08$ rad/s just after impact. Energy is not conserved because the impact is plastic.

blocks.markdown: **Centre of percussion.** A body pinned at O is struck by an impulse $J$ perpendicular to the line from O to its centre of mass G (distance $d_G$), applied at distance $q$ from O. The pin impulse is zero when the linear momentum change $J=m d_G\omega$ and the angular momentum change $Jq=I_O\omega$ both hold with no pin force. Eliminating $J$ and $\omega$ gives the location of the **centre of percussion**.

blocks.caption: $k_G$ is the radius of gyration about G. For a uniform bar pivoted at one end, $d_G=L/2$ and $q=\tfrac23L$.

blocks.title: Centre of percussion of a pivoted bar
blocks.prompt: A uniform bar of length 1.0 m is pivoted at a point 0.10 m from one end. Find the centre of percussion measured from the pivot.

steps.text: The centre is 0.50 m from the end, so $d_G=0.50-0.10=0.40$ m. Centroidal radius of gyration squared.

blocks.answer: $q=0.608$ m from the pivot on the side of G, so a blow there produces no pin impulse.

rows: Conservation of angular momentum about O
Only forces through O during impact
Pivoted body struck, pin impulse zero
blocks.caption: Impulsive methods for rigid bodies.

blocks.title: Significance of the centre of percussion
blocks.text: Striking (or catching) at the centre of percussion gives the pin, hand or support no impulse. This is why the 'sweet spot' of a bat or hammer does not sting, and why impact testers and swinging pendulums place the support relative to the point of impact.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.text: Conserving linear momentum for a pinned body, using $I_G$ instead of $I_O$ with the pin as the axis, forgetting to include the lump mass $m_pd^2$ when it sticks, and using rev/min rather than rad/s.

points: Angular impulse about a fixed axis equals the change in angular momentum: $\int M\,dt=I\Delta\omega$.
For a pinned body struck by a particle, angular momentum about the pin is conserved: $m_pvd=(I_O+m_pd^2)\omega$ if the particle sticks.
The centre of percussion $q=I_O/(m d_G)$ is the impact point at which the pin receives no impulse.

questions.stem: A small ball strikes a uniform bar that is hinged at one end. Which quantity is conserved for the ball-and-bar system during the very short impact?

options.text: Angular momentum about the centre of the bar

distractorRationale.b: The hinge applies a large impulsive force, so linear momentum is not conserved.
distractorRationale.c: Unless the impact is perfectly elastic, kinetic energy is lost.
distractorRationale.d: The hinge impulse has a moment about the bar's centre, so this is not conserved.

questions.explanation: The hinge force passes through the hinge and has zero moment about it, so the moment of momentum about the hinge is unchanged. Linear momentum and energy are not in general conserved.

questions.stem: A uniform bar (2 kg, 0.80 m long) hangs from a pin at its top end. A 0.05 kg ball moving horizontally at 40 m/s hits the lower end and sticks to it. Find the angular velocity of the bar immediately afterwards in rad/s.
A flywheel of moment of inertia 2.5 kg m$^2$ starts from rest. A net angular impulse of 150 N m s is applied. What is its final angular velocity?

distractorRationale.a: This multiplies impulse by $I$ instead of dividing.
distractorRationale.b: This equals the impulse and forgets to divide by $I$.

questions.explanation: The principle gives $\int M\,dt=I\omega_2$, so $\omega_2=150/2.5=60$ rad/s, about 573 rev/min.

questions.stem: A flywheel with $I=1.8$ kg m$^2$ turns at 300 rev/min. A brake applies a constant torque of 8 N m for 4 s, with no other torques acting. Find its angular velocity in rad/s after the braking.
questions.explanation: Initial speed $\omega_1=300(2\pi)/60=31.42$ rad/s. The angular impulse of the brake is $-8(4)=-32$ N m s, so $\omega_2=31.42-32/1.8=31.42-17.78=13.64$ rad/s.

questions.stem: A uniform bar of length 0.90 m is pivoted at a point 0.15 m from one end. Where, measured from the pivot, is its centre of percussion?

distractorRationale.a: This is half the bar length, the distance from the centre of mass to either end, not the location of the centre of percussion.
distractorRationale.c: This is $\tfrac23L$ for a pivot at the end of the bar.
distractorRationale.d: This is only the term $k_G^2/d_G$ and omits $d_G$.

questions.stem: A particle of mass $m_p$ and speed $v$ strikes, perpendicular to a pinned body, at distance $d$ from the pin and sticks to it. The body has $I_O$ about the pin. Which expression gives the angular velocity just after impact?

distractorRationale.b: This treats the problem as a linear momentum conservation.
distractorRationale.c: This ignores the added inertia of the particle after it sticks.
distractorRationale.d: This has the wrong dimensions for angular velocity.

questions.explanation: Conservation of angular momentum about the pin gives $m_pvd=(I_O+m_pd^2)\omega$. The stuck particle contributes $m_pd^2$ to the total inertia.

questions.stem: A uniform bar (3 kg, 1.0 m long) hangs from a pin at its top end. A 0.1 kg ball hits the bottom end horizontally at 30 m/s and rebounds at 10 m/s in the opposite direction. Find the bar's angular velocity just after the impact in rad/s.
questions.explanation: Angular momentum about the pin: $0.1(30)(1.0)=-0.1(10)(1.0)+I_O\omega$ with $I_O=\tfrac13(3)(1.0)^2=1.0$ kg m$^2$. So $\omega=(3.0+1.0)/1.0=4.0$ rad/s.

questions.stem: A hammer is modelled as a rigid body pivoted at the user's grip. At which point on the hammer should the blow be delivered so that the grip receives no impulsive force?

options.text: At the centre of percussion, beyond the centre of mass as seen from the grip
At the point farthest from the grip regardless of geometry

questions.correctOptionText: At the centre of percussion, beyond the centre of mass as seen from the grip

distractorRationale.b: A blow at G gives pure translation, and the grip must supply a reaction impulse to stop it turning about the grip.
distractorRationale.c: The blow would act through the pin and be entirely carried by the grip.
distractorRationale.d: Only one particular distance, $q=I_O/(md_G)$, gives zero grip impulse.

questions.explanation: At the centre of percussion the linear and angular impulse equations are satisfied simultaneously with zero pin impulse. This point lies at $q=I_O/(md_G)$, farther from the pivot than G.

questions.stem: Starting from $\sum M_O=I_O\alpha$, derive the angular impulse-momentum principle for fixed-axis rotation. A flywheel ($I=2.0$ kg m$^2$) is at rest and receives a triangular torque pulse rising from 0 to 80 N m in 0.25 s and falling to 0 in a further 0.25 s. Find the final angular velocity.
markingGuide: Recognises impulse as the area under the torque-time graph
questions.explanation: Because $I$ is constant, the integral of $I\,d\omega/dt$ is $I\Delta\omega$. The triangle has base 0.50 s and height 80 N m.

questions.stem: Derive the location of the centre of percussion of a body of mass $m$ pivoted at O with centre of mass a distance $d_G$ from O, and explain why it matters in the design of hammers, bats and pendulum impact testers.
markingGuide: Impulse $J$ at distance $q$ from O perpendicular to OG
Linear impulse equation with zero pin impulse: $J=md_G\omega$
Significance: a blow here produces no pin reaction impulse, so no sting in the hand, no bearing shock; for a uniform end-pivoted bar $q=2L/3$
questions.explanation: $q$ is always greater than $d_G$ because $k_G^2/d_G>0$, so the centre of percussion lies beyond the centre of mass from the pivot.
